subsystems.name: Alloy design
subsystems.role: find a composition that resists crystallising when cooled.

subsystems.name: Melting and melt handling
subsystems.role: turn solid elements into a clean, homogeneous liquid.

subsystems.name: Rapid solidification
subsystems.role: freeze the liquid before atoms can arrange into crystals.

subsystems.name: Forming and shaping
subsystems.role: make the final part without recrystallising it.
parts: thermoplastic forming in the supercooled liquid region

subsystems.name: Quality control
subsystems.role: prove the part is truly amorphous and meets strength specs.

buildSteps.title: Design the alloy
buildSteps.detail: Combine three or more elements in proportions that create a deep eutectic, lowering the critical cooling rate needed to avoid crystals.

buildSteps.title: Melt the charge
buildSteps.detail: High-purity elements are melted together in vacuum or inert gas to prevent oxidation and contamination.

buildSteps.title: Quench to a glass
buildSteps.detail: For ribbon, a stream of melt hits a spinning copper wheel and solidifies in milliseconds; for bulk parts, the melt is pressure-cast into a water-cooled copper mould.

buildSteps.title: Confirm amorphous structure
buildSteps.detail: X-ray diffraction shows a broad halo instead of sharp crystal peaks, and calorimetry reveals the glass transition.

buildSteps.title: Shape the part
buildSteps.detail: Bulk glass can be softened in its supercooled liquid region and pressed into a mould, or cast near-net shape; final dimensions are finished by grinding or diamond turning.

buildSteps.title: Relieve stress
buildSteps.detail: A low-temperature anneal below the glass transition relaxes internal stresses without causing crystallisation.

buildSteps.title: Assemble
buildSteps.detail: Parts are joined by welding, soldering or adhesives, taking care not to heat the glass above its crystallisation temperature.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: Strength, hardness, corrosion and fatigue tests confirm the part behaves as designed.

prerequisites.why: cooling fast enough is the defining requirement.
trial-and-error still dominates the search for new bulk glasses.
shaping and assembling without crystallising remains difficult.
thick parts cool slowly and crystallise, limiting bulk metallic glasses to small components.

pathway.milestone: iron-based amorphous ribbon in transformer cores; small bulk-glass parts in watches, golf clubs and medical tools
pathway.unlocks: low-loss magnetic components and hard, corrosion-resistant small parts.

pathway.milestone: additive manufacturing and new compositions for larger bulk parts
pathway.unlocks: complex structural components that stay amorphous.

pathway.milestone: ductile bulk glasses with controlled toughness
pathway.unlocks: use in aerospace and automotive structures.

pathway.milestone: cost-effective continuous production of thick sections
pathway.unlocks: widespread structural use as a lightweight, strong material.
